𝐌𝐌𝐃𝐀 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐖𝐚𝐥𝐤-𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡 𝐀𝐡𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐓𝐫𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐏𝐞𝐬𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐡

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) conducted a coordinated walk-through at the People Power Monument earlier today in connection with the “Trillion Peso Movement March”. 

The activity aimed to ensure public safety, unhampered vehicular traffic flow, and uphold peace and order in the vicinity of the monument and adjacent roads on February 25.

Upon the directive of MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, MMDA General Manager Usec. Nicolas Torre III reiterated that the walk-through is part of the agency’s standard operating procedure for mass gatherings, particularly those held in high-traffic corridors and historically significant public spaces to ensure the safety of participants and the general public while keeping major roads passable. 

“Our priority is to ensure that the participants of this activity and the general public is safe while making sure that our major roads are passable. We respect the right of citizens to assemble peacefully, and we are committed to providing the necessary support to maintain order,” Torre said.

“The MMDA continuously reaffirms its commitment to coordinating closely with Quezon City LGU, law enforcement agencies, and event organizers to ensure that public gatherings are conducted safely and responsibly,” he added.

The inspection included determining entry and exit points, emergency access lanes, and identifying alternate routes to cushion the effect on traffic.

The Trillion Peso Movement March Part 3 will take place on Wednesday, February 25. Participants will gather at the EDSA Shrine for a 7:00 a.m. prayer then proceed to the People Power Monument, followed by afternoon activities and programs. This will be participated by Tindig Pilipinas, Partido Manggagawa, other groups and sectors in society, with an anticipated crowd of 30,000.

The MMDA will deploy traffic enforcers at key choke points and establish designated rerouting schemes for both private and public utility vehicles. Emergency lanes will be clearly marked and kept unobstructed to allow immediate access for medical responders and law enforcement units if necessary. 

Equipment such as ambulances, tow trucks, dump trucks for clearing, portalets, plastic cones and barriers, mobile patrol units, motorcycle units, and among others will also be dispatched to designated areas.

Motorists are advised to expect slightly heavier traffic on the day of the activity due to the anticipated influx of participants and vehicles in nearby areas. However, the MMDA has assured the public that no road closures will be implemented along EDSA, which will remain fully passable throughout the day, as it has been officially declared a No Rally Zone.

#mmda #mmdaatyourservice
